root.title: Opt-in request correlation IDs
root.objective: Plan an integrated Express change that provides opt-in request identity, response propagation, focused tests, and public documentation while preserving default compatibility.

outcomes.description: When enabled, requests expose a preserved or securely generated ID and responses return the same X-Request-Id.
Applications that do not enable correlation IDs retain their current request and response behavior.
The public configuration and req.id property are documented with focused coverage.

cut.rationale: Configuration, request identity, response propagation, tests, and documentation have distinct owners and proof strategies but must integrate through explicit opt-in and identity seams.

children.title: Opt-in configuration
children.objective: Plan the application-owned setting so correlation IDs are explicitly enabled and disabled behavior remains unchanged.

outcomes.description: Correlation IDs are disabled by default and controlled through explicit application configuration.

verification.rationale: Exercise both disabled baseline behavior and explicit enablement.

children.title: Request identity
children.objective: Plan request-owned preservation of a valid incoming X-Request-Id or secure platform generation and expose the stable value as req.id.

outcomes.description: An enabled request exposes one stable req.id derived from a valid incoming value or a secure Node.js platform primitive.

verification.rationale: Cover incoming preservation, generated identity, stability, and handler visibility.

children.title: Response propagation
children.objective: Plan response-owned emission of X-Request-Id using the exact request identity while preserving disabled response behavior.

outcomes.description: An enabled response emits X-Request-Id with the same value exposed as req.id.

verification.rationale: Compare the handler-visible request ID with the emitted response header.

children.title: Focused request-ID tests
children.objective: Plan focused request and response cases for enabled behavior, incoming preservation, secure generation, identity equality, and disabled negative controls.

outcomes.description: Focused executable tests cover request-ID behavior and the disabled baseline across request and response owners.

verification.rationale: Run the focused authored cases through the registered deterministic procedure.

children.title: Public documentation
children.objective: Plan documentation for enabling correlation IDs, using req.id, preserving incoming X-Request-Id, generating IDs, emitting the response header, and retaining unchanged defaults.

outcomes.description: The public opt-in setting and req.id behavior are documented, including incoming, generated, and response-header behavior.

seams.purpose: Carry the application-owned opt-in decision into request identity resolution.

interface.promise: Request identity remains inactive unless the application explicitly enables correlation IDs.
interface.compatibility: Disabled applications preserve existing request and response behavior and no runtime dependency is introduced.

verification.rationale: Prove explicit enablement and the protected disabled baseline.

seams.purpose: Carry the exact stable req.id value to X-Request-Id response emission.

interface.promise: The response header equals the preserved or securely generated value exposed as req.id.
interface.compatibility: The seam is exact when enabled and introduces no correlation header behavior when disabled.

verification.rationale: Compare request-visible identity and the emitted response header.
